 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. After making it to the NBA Finals last season, the San Antonio Spurs did not lose a single rotation player in the offseason. In fact, they added Tobias Harris in free agency, who averaged an efficient 13.3 points for the Detroit Pistons last season.
 As expected, the Spurs have taken a step forward from last year and are atop the Western Conference standings. Winners of 12 games in a row, they are pretty clearly the best team in the NBA.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement However, Harris is yet to make his debut. He missed the preseason and was questionable for the season opener against the OKC Thunder with a calf strain, and his return has continuously been pushed back. It's gotten to the point where fans are unsure when he will step out onto the floor, although when he does, the team is expected to get another boost.

 What to Expect from Tobias Harris
 Remember, at the very start of the season, he was ruled out day-to-day. His debut has been pushed back several months at this point, but it could be around the corner.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement "I'm told he is getting better," reported Chris Haynes. "He can make his season debut as early as early December."
 Harris has been a full-time starter for various teams over the last nine seasons. With Victor Wembanyama, Devin Vassell, De'Aaron Fox, Dylan Harper, and Stephon Castle, the Spurs have the NBA's best starting five, and there's no room to add Harris.
 Expect him to come off the bench for the entire season, even after he's 100 percent healthy.
 "The starting lineup should not change," summed up The Athletic's Jared Weiss. "Devin Vassell has been the right fit for that grouping from the beginning. The Spurs have three guards handling the ball and a center in Wembanyama who works with the ball in his hands all the time, so the fifth guy in that group needs to be someone who can play without the ball, live above the rim and run a lot. That's Vassell's strength. And because Castle and Harper defensively have pretty good strength, they need more of an athletic speed defender than they do someone of Harris' size. Where the Spurs need help is the second unit, and that's where Harris, who hasn't played this season because of a calf strain, and Kornet come in."
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Behind Vassell, the Spurs have full faith in Julian Champagnie. Harris might be the sixth man; he might be the tenth man. Behind the starting five, the rotation isn't as clear-cut.
 All fans can hope for is that he's soon aviliable and productive.
